subject: Problems Analyzing 100k: "Cannot fit target function to enzyme"

messages.author: 4734f864c8ec0a5b
messages.subject: Problems Analyzing 100k: "Cannot fit target function to enzyme"
parts:
Hi!, I´m new analyzing affymetrix 100k chip, I´m following the next
script:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("Oscar_Set_100k",
chipType="Mapping50K_Hind240")
qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs)
csQN <- process(qn, verbose=TRUE)
plm <- RmaCnPlm(csQN, combineAlleles=TRUE, mergeStrands=TRUE)
fit(plm, verbose=TRUE)
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces)
cesN <- process(fln, verbose=TRUE)

glad <- GladModel(cesN)
ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(glad)
process(ce, verbose=-3)

But, when I try to run: cesN <- process(fln, verbose=TRUE)
I´m getting the following exception:

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Problems Analyzing 100k: "Cannot fit target function to enzyme"
parts:
Hi "sc@rcega",

I suspect that the fit(plm, verbose=TRUE) step was never
done/completed. This was the cause of an almost identical problem
discussed last week, cf. Thread 'about: wrong information of CN 500k'
on Nov 6, 2008:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/6dfe3afc216f27fc/34442574ee1b039a

Note, it's helpful if you increase the verbosity of the output
message, i.e. use verbose=-20 or similar (verbose=TRUE corresponds to
verbose=-1). That will give you more details on what is going on
before you get an error message, and you can do a better job on
troubleshoothing.

Hope this helps

Henrik
